## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sabbamidaṁkammatotikathā* (Kv 17.3) is a debate text in the seventeenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. The text examines and refutes the proposition that "all this is due to karma" (*sabbam idaṁ kammato*), repudiating the doctrine that all phenomena, including ongoing karmic actions themselves, are determined solely by previous karma; as noted by modern scholarship, rejecting this premise was essential to avoid an untenable strict determinism and an infinite regress [Waldron 2003]. The SuttaCentral database links this discourse to the *Vāseṭṭha Sutta* (MN 98) [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallel texts in other languages are cataloged by SuttaCentral, though it lists one translation of the text [SuttaCentral]. Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 111 matching passages across 12 Pali texts, reflecting shared dialectical formulations with other chapters of the *Kathāvatthu*, most substantially the *Kammūpacayakathā* (Kv 15.11), the *Dānakathā* (Kv 7.4), and the *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), along with minor formulaic overlap with the *Madhura Sutta* (MN 84) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also identifies machine alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan works, including the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and the Tibetan *Vinayapraśnaṭīkā* (D4135) [DharmaNexus].
